name: CO2 electroreduction to CO, formic acid and ethylene
principle: CO2 is reduced at a cathode to CO (Ag, Au), formate (Pb, Sn) or ethylene (Cu). Kenis and colleagues report CO at 94% Faradaic efficiency and 91 mA/cm2 on a silver gas-diffusion electrode and say commercial use needs overpotential below 0.2 V at above 100 mA/cm2; no standard durability protocols existed in 2013.

process_steps.name: CO2 and water or electrolyte feed

performance.metric: CO faradaic efficiency on Ag GDE

source.note: Jhong, Ma and Kenis, Electrochemical conversion of CO2 to useful chemicals (review, 2013)
Jhong, Ma and Kenis, Electrochemical conversion of CO2 to useful chemicals (review, 2013)

advantages: Direct CO2 conversion with renewable power
limitations: 2013 review: durability and cost models lacking
High FE, EE and current density are rarely all achieved together

costs.basis: Low-temperature CO2 electrolysis at 4,000 full-load hours: CO 5.1 EUR/kg, formate 3.7, ethylene 60. Investment is over 60% of the levelised cost. Per kg of product, not per tonne of CO2.
